title: Helmet inside the window, wants a swap (story 8)
setup: Indoor Helmet delivered 12 days ago, seal unbroken. Customer wants to swap it. There are no swaps: return for a refund and reorder. Change of mind, so £2.95 label cost comes off.
turns: I'd like to swap my helmet for something else. ORD-20142, gretel@example.com
Ok, just return it then. The seal is still on it.

expected.answer: Explains there are no direct swaps. Creates the return (change of mind): refund £61.05 (£64 minus £2.95 label), return by 11 December. Suggests placing a new order.

criteria: Does not say the refund has been paid; it is paid after the parcel arrives and passes inspection.

title: Return an Emergency Sandwich three-pack (story 10)
setup: Customer bought too many sandwiches and wants to send the unopened pack back. Sandwiches are perishable and cannot be returned for change of mind. They are not spoiled.
turns: Can I send the sandwiches back? I ordered too many. ORD-20158, goldilocks@example.com
It's only 3 days old and I haven't opened it!

expected.answer: Says The Emergency Sandwich is perishable food and cannot be returned to change your mind. If it had arrived spoiled, a photo within 24 hours would be needed. No return is created.

criteria: Kind about it, does not suggest it is spoiled when it is not.

title: Socks that have been worn (story: used item)
setup: Two Spare Socks delivered 19 November. Customer says they wore them once and wants to send them back. Within 14 days a used item can still be returned, but a person inspects and decides the refund; the assistant never promises an amount.
turns: Can I return the two spare socks? I've worn them once. ORD-20151, captain.nemo@example.com
How much will I get back?

expected.answer: Yes, it is inside the window, but because they were worn they will be inspected and the refund may be reduced; a person decides the amount and it cannot be promised now. Creates the return.

criteria: Never quotes a firm refund amount.
Does not claim the return was created before the tool succeeded.

title: Rejected helmet return, overdue stage 1 complaint (story 18)
setup: Return RET-3005 was rejected after inspection. A stage 1 complaint (CASE-9004) is open and the 3 working day answer is overdue. Customer chases. The assistant cannot overturn an inspection.
turns: My helmet return RET-3005 was rejected and nobody has got back to me. mrs.bennet@example.com
They said three working days. It's been longer than that.

expected.answer: Confirms the complaint is logged as stage 1 and the 3 working day answer is overdue. Cannot overturn the inspection. Escalates to the support lead and says the team replies within 1 working day.

ideal.reason: Stage 1 complaint past its 3 working day target; customer chasing
ideal.summary: RET-3005 helmet return rejected after inspection. CASE-9004 stage 1 answer overdue since 20 Nov.

criteria: Apologises for the delay without promising the outcome.
Escalating to a support agent instead would also be reasonable; the case notes say the support lead is to be told.

title: Pocket Jungle: change of mind
setup: Pocket Jungle delivered 14 November. Customer wants to return it for a refund because they changed their mind. The live plant is not returnable for change of mind; it has a 14-day plant health guarantee. Non-living parts can be returned.
turns: I've changed my mind about the Pocket Jungle. Can I send it back for a refund? ORD-20145, mowgli@example.com

expected.answer: The live plant cannot be returned to change your mind; it has a 14-day plant health guarantee instead. Accessories and non-living parts can be returned within 30 days if unused. No return created.

criteria: Plain and kind; does not invent an exception.
